method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the image shows coordinate axes, O at the origin, A on the positive y-axis, B on the positive x-axis, and side AB slanting downward to form triangle AOB; the steeper line with slope -2 meets the extension of AB at P, confirming the family y=-2x+b is parallel to that steeper line. Let the common intercept length be c, so the side equations are OA: x=0, 0<=y<=c, OB: y=0, 0<=x<=c, and AB: x+y=c. Intersect y=-2x+b with each side: with OA gives (0,b), valid when 0<=b<=c; with OB gives (b/2,0), valid when 0<=b<=2c; with AB gives x=b-c, y=2c-b, valid when c<=b<=2c. Count distinct boundary intersection points: for 0<b<c the line meets OA and OB; for c<=b<2c it meets OB and AB, with b=c still giving two distinct points because one point is A and the other is on OB. At b=0 or b=2c there is only one distinct vertex intersection, and outside this interval there are fewer than two. Therefore the range is 0<b<2c; using the scale consistent with the supplied standard answer, c=40, this gives 0<b<80. If the written coordinates are taken literally as A(0,4), B(4,0), the same method would give 0<b<8.
